answer: Each identity is verified by a Wesolowski VDF: repeated modular squaring makes each step depend on the previous one, so a single proof has a sequential time cost that GPUs cannot shorten through parallel execution. An attacker can run clone computations concurrently, but must pay that cost separately for each clone; the kernel cannot be shared, and a mirror identity adds its own delay and work. A delta in available hardware may raise throughput, not erase the per-identity bottleneck.
